text:
izzy: Heads up — saw a sharp increase in dropped StatsD metrics and token-level latency on /generate after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout. :eyes:
izzy: Token P50 ~ unchanged but P95/P99 jumped ~2.2x; per-route KPI dashboard shows /generate is the outlier.
ajay: ugh, did the kernel selector change also flip any batching heuristics or KV prefetching flags?
izzy: Yes — selector now prefers relu-optimized kernels for sequence lengths <= 256, and we switched to aggressive prefetch during KV warmups.
maria: I pulled a short flamegraph from the canary node — kernel switch itself seems fine but there's a lot of time in 'kv_prefetch::wait_for_batch' and 'statsd::emit_sync' in the hot path.
ken: can you paste the flame snippet?
maria: ```
flamegraph: 34% kernel_exec
           28% kv_prefetch::wait_for_batch
           18% statsd::emit_sync
           10% scheduler::spin_wait
```
ajay: statsd::emit_sync on hot path is bad — we should be using async batching for metrics. Did the exporter config change?
izzy: Not intentionally. But I see in the canary config the OTEL exporter env var is unset, falling back to legacy statsd with socket timeout 200ms. That explains the sync retries.
metrics-bot: [alert] statsd_exporter.dropped_count increased by 457 in 5m for cluster:runtime-canary
maria: Also the KV prefetch increased the # of inter-op waits — because kernel switch reduced per-token compute time, IO/metrics glue became visible.
ken: So two contributors: (1) synchronous metrics emission causing tail delays and dropbacks; (2) KV prefetch contention due to more aggressive batching.
ajay: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert prefetch aggressiveness to previous thresholds and flip statsd to async buffer mode. We can patch live via feature flags.
izzy: I've opened a canary patch: ```/flags/runtime.prefetch_aggressiveness=0.6``` -> previous was 0.3. Also pushed statsd change: ```STATS_SYNC=false; METRICS_BUFFER=2000``` to canary. deploy-bot: canary rollout to 30% completed (deploy 2026-02-12T14:18Z).
maria: Can we also add per-token emit sampling so non-essential per-token counters are sampled 1/10? That should remove steady-state pressure.
ken: +1 for sampling. Also we need a short-term backfill plan for the dropped metrics so dashboards match.
ajay: Backfill plan idea: reprocess raw event logs for last 6h and re-emit metrics to the long-term pipeline with tag backfill=true. Job name: metrics-backfill/runtime-canary/6h.
izzy: I'll kick off a dry-run reemit for a 10m window to validate transformations. Assigning: izzy -> run dry run; ajay -> patch statsd exporter for async + sampling; maria -> monitor flamegraphs and KV metrics; ken -> prepare backfill job template and quotas.
maria: Dry-run results: reemit succeeded for 10m window, no dup suppression triggered. We need to ensure the backfill job sets metric_source=backfill to avoid double-counting in billing views.
ken: Good catch. Will add metric_source tag. Also suggest we throttle reemit to keep write QPS < 500/s to avoid overloading OTEL ingest.
ajay: Small config diff I'm going to apply to prod after canary looks stable: ```diff
- STATS_SYNC=true
- METRICS_BUFFER=200
+ STATS_SYNC=false
+ METRICS_BUFFER=2000
+ METRIC_SAMPLING_RATE=0.1
```
izzy: After the flag flip on canary the P99 on /generate dropped back ~30% in the last 12m. Dropped statsd count stabilized.
metrics-bot: [info] backfill job queued: metrics-backfill/runtime-canary/6h (est run 45m)
ken: Next steps: keep canary for 1 hour, if stable promote kernel-selector change + statsd async to 100%. Start backfill after promotion.
maria: I'll keep an eye on KV stall graphs and publish a lightweight dashboard showing kv_prefetch_wait/requests and statsd_latency per host.
ajay: Thanks all. If anything wiggles, revert selector to previous commit id abc123 and re-run tests.
izzy: I'll post a short postmortem once backfill completes and metrics are reconciled — including timeline, root causes (metrics sync + prefetch), and follow-ups (sampling by default, async emitter guardrail). :shipit:
